# vantable

> Zero-dependency vanilla-JS data table for dashboards. One UMD file (works as a
> `<script>` global, an ESM import or a CommonJS require), no jQuery, no
> Bootstrap, no XLSX library. The default stylesheet is injected from the script
> itself, so a table is styled with nothing else included.

Version: 0.2.0 · License: MIT · Runtime dependencies: none.

## Install

    npm i vantable
    import Vantable from 'vantable'            // ESM
    const Vantable = require('vantable')       // CJS
    <script src="https://unpkg.com/vantable/dist/vantable.umd.js"></script>

Entry points: `main`/`require` → `src/vantable.js`, `module`/`import` →
`src/vantable.mjs`, `browser`/`unpkg`/`jsdelivr` → `dist/vantable.umd.js`,
`types` → `src/vantable.d.ts`, `vantable/css` → `src/vantable.css` (only needed
with `styles: false`).

## Quick start

    const table = new Vantable('#host', {
      columns: [
        { key: 'id',     label: 'ID',     type: 'number', width: '60px' },
        { key: 'name',   label: 'Name',   editable: true },
        { key: 'email',  label: 'Email',  type: 'copy' },
        { key: 'status', label: 'Status', type: 'status',
          map: { 1: { label: 'On', color: '#22a06b' }, 2: { label: 'Off', color: '#e35d4b' } } },
        { label: 'Actions', type: 'actions', edit: { enabled: true }, remove: { enabled: true } }
      ],
      data: rows,
      search: 'live',
      pagination: { perPage: 25 },
      onSave: (id, changes) => save(id, changes)
    });

## Options (constructor, second argument)

- columns (required): array of column definitions, `'key'` strings or
  `[key, label]` tuples.
- data: client-side rows. rowId: the id field (default `'id'`).
- search / sort: `'live'|'client'|'local'` (in the browser), `'server'|'db'|
  'remote'` (through `server.fetch`), `false`. Default follows the source.
- searchFields: which keys the global search looks at (default: all data columns).
- defaultSort, defaultDir: the starting order.
- pagination: `false` or `{ perPage, options }` (default 50 / 50-100-250-500).
- server: `{ fetch({ page, perPage, q, fields, sort, dir, filters }) -> { rows, total } }`.
- editable + onSave(id, changes, row): inline row editing.
- actions: `{ edit, remove, custom, menu }` when not using an `actions` column.
- actions.remove.url goes to fetch verbatim — nothing is encoded, so wrap row
  values yourself: `url: r => '/api/users/' + encodeURIComponent(r.id)`.
  destroy() also closes the confirmation dialog if one is open.
- actions.remove.confirm: `{ title, className, overlayClassName, bodyClassName,
  footClassName, cancelClassName, confirmClassName }` — the look of the delete
  dialog. The classes are ADDED to the built-in `.vt-modal*` ones. The dialog
  hangs off <body>, so the tokens and typography the table resolves to are
  copied onto `.vt-modal-overlay` inline when it opens — it matches the table,
  not the page. With both `options.actions` and an actions column, the former
  wins and the column's `remove` is not read.
- accordion: `{ render(row) }` or `{ columns: [...] }` — master/detail rows.
- export: `true` or `{ formats, filename, adapters: { csv, xlsx, pdf } }`.
- printable, exportName, emptyText, label, labelledby, labels (i18n).
- styles: true (built-in CSS, default) | false (none) | '<css text>' (yours
  instead) | { css, href, extend } — `extend: true` keeps the built-in sheet
  under yours. The same CSS is injected once per page.
- filters: `true | 'client' | 'server' | false` — mode of the per-column filters
  (columns opt in with their own `filter`).
- selection: `true` or `{ mode:'multi'|'single', header, selectable(row), actions }`.
- states: `true` or `{ loading, skeleton, error, retry }` — async states, on by default.
- virtual: `true` or `{ rowHeight, overscan }` — render only the rows in view.
- responsive: `true` or `{ breakpoint }` — stack rows into cards when narrow.
- resize, reorder, columnPicker, stickyHeader, maxHeight, minColWidth — column ops.
- keyboard (default true), styles (default true), theme, mode: 'dark'|'light'.

## Column definition

Common: key (dotted paths work), label, type, sortable, searchable, editable,
align, width, className, cellClass, prefix, suffix, filter, pin ('left'|'right'),
hidden, resizable, reorderable.

Types and their own props:
- text / number — plain value
- link — href (string or row => url), target, text
- external — opens in a new tab, always rel="noopener"
- copy — value plus a copy-to-clipboard button
- status — map: { value: { label, color } } → coloured badge
- select / tag — options: [{ value, label }], onChange(row, value)
- image — src (string or row => url)
- download — filename, text; saves the cell value as a file
- html — render(value, row) → raw markup (the ONLY unescaped path)
- actions — edit, remove (remove.confirm restyles its dialog), custom[], menu

Everything except `html` (and an accordion `render()`) is HTML-escaped.

## Methods

setData(rows), refresh(), exportCsv(name), print(), scrollToRow(i), destroy(),
on(event, cb), setLoading(on), setError(err|null),
toggleColumn/hideColumn/showColumn(key), moveColumn(key, index),
setColumnWidth(key, w), pinColumn(key, 'left'|'right'|false), columnOrder(),
columnState(), setColumnState(snapshot),
setFilter(key, value), getFilter(key), filters(), activeFilters(), clearFilters(),
selectRow(id, on), selectAll(), clearSelection(), selectedIds(), selectedRows(),
selectedCount(), isSelected(id), isStacked().

Statics: Vantable.version, Vantable.css, Vantable.injectStyles(),
Vantable.serverExport(url, opts), Vantable.sheetJsExport(opts),
Vantable.jsPdfExport(opts).

## Events (table.on(name, cb))

render, save, remove, edit, action, cellChange, expand, copy, export, error,
destroy, columnResize, columnMove, columnPin, columnVisibility, virtualRange,
loading, selectionChange, bulkAction, filterChange, responsive.

## Things worth knowing

- Zero runtime dependencies. XLSX/PDF need an adapter you choose; SheetJS and
  jsPDF are never bundled, and `tools/vtexport` is a separate Go CLI.
- The CSS lives in two places that must stay in sync: `src/vantable.css` and the
  `DEFAULT_CSS` string inside the library. `dist/vantable.umd.js` is a byte copy
  of `src/vantable.js` (`npm run build`).
- Virtualization needs a bounded scroll box (`maxHeight`); it is ignored with an
  accordion and pauses in the responsive card mode, because both break the
  uniform row height it relies on.
- A failed `server.fetch` shows an error row; `states: { error: false }` brings
  back the plain empty row. A synchronous throw from `server.fetch` is NOT
  caught — reject instead.
- Selection is keyed by row id and survives search, sort, paging and refreshes;
  `selectedRows()` can only resolve the rows currently loaded.
- Exports cover the filtered/sorted view (the fetched page in server mode), not
  the rows hidden by column visibility.
- All user-facing text comes from `labels`; override any subset to translate.

## Repository layout

src/vantable.js (the library), src/vantable.css, src/vantable.d.ts,
src/vantable.mjs, dist/vantable.umd.js, examples/index.html (9 live demos),
test/*.test.mjs (Node test runner + jsdom), tools/vtexport (Go export CLI).
